claims.criteria: 'Best jeans fit' is defined as the reader's own most workable combination of secure waist, comfortable movement, intended leg shape and suitable hem; it is not a superiority claim about Spykar or a product ranking.
claims.statement: The article helps each reader identify their best personal fit through a consistent in-store comparison routine.

claims.statement: The new article should target the in-store trial and store-discovery intent rather than publish another general taxonomy of denim fits.

detector_notes.note: The complete publishable body, excluding repository frontmatter, image handoff markup and FAQ JSON-LD, was checked on the live ZeroGPT website. ZeroGPT labelled the text 'Human written' and reported 12% AI/GPT. This is recorded as a weak editorial risk signal, not proof of authorship.

sources.extracted_facts: Spykar is an India-focused denim-led youth brand. Blog copy uses Indian English, practical fit and styling detail, natural unbolded keywords, restrained claims, the canonical native Google Doc structure and a soft CTA.
Requested title and phrases: How to Find Your Best Jeans Fit In-Store in 10 Minutes; spykar store near me; spykar showroom near me; denim fits guide; how to choose jeans fit.

Local keyword records map 'spykar showroom near me' and 'spykar store near me' to the store-locator intent and record 2026 GSC rows; 'denim fits guide' is an informational seed. The article does not convert these rows into unverified ranking or conversion claims.

Top-three relevant organic review: Levi's India rendered at 859 words with fit-by-fit H2 sections; Naked & Famous rendered at 944 words with men/women fit comparison and measurement guidance; Who What Wear rendered at 2,884 words with named-editor tips and product picks. The combined benchmark favours direct advice, a scannable sequence and approximately 1,800–2,100 useful words for the distinct in-store intent.
Spykar already has broad men's-fit, every-fit and modern men-and-women fit explainers. None is organised as a ten-minute in-store trial-room routine tied to local store discovery.
The official page at /pages/store-locator returned HTTP 200 and displayed a location field plus list/map modes. The older /a/storelocator URL returned HTTP 404 and is not used in the article.
